                                    Recommendations:

                                    1. Instructions be issued to investigating Air Force personnel to
                                    remain completely objective in the reporting and recording of observed
•
                                    data. The distortion of the true orientation of the ~vo larger
                                    footprints would have been very misleading had the photographs not
                                    been available to show them to be located in other than symmetrical
            •
                                    manner •

                                    2. It is suggested that an appointed member o:f the civil engineering
                                    personnel of each Air Force Base be given a very brief course in
                                    obtaj,ning soil sampl.es and taking soi1 strength data readings. Capt.
                                    Skillen, AFIT/CEC, has suggested that this course could be given to
                                    such personnel during their regularly scheduled periods. o£ instruc-
                                    tion at the Air Force Institute of Technology at WPAFB. In this     '
                                    manner, a more accurate estimated weight acting on the depressions
                                    can be made in the investigation of future reported sightings.

                                    For instance, . it is highly desirable that cone penetrometer (or other
                                    similar tests) be performed at a number of stations in the immediate                                                                                              •
                                    vicinity of the depressions as well as within the depression itsel£.
                                    In this manner, the strength of the undisturbed soil would be estab-
                                    lished as well as the degree of compression of the soil under the
                                    footprint area.
    •
                                    3.  It is mandatory that a more accurate layout of the footprint
        •
                                    locations and orientation be made. Pieces of string tied between                                                                                                      I

                                    pegs can serve as valuable reference lines. At the mjnimum, a
                               •
                                    base line should be drawn by scribing a straight line in a conven-
                                    ient location on the soil. All poin~s would then be referenced
                                    from this line so that an accurate diagram can be reconstructed of
                                    the site by participating investigators. Photographs of the site
                                    should include ~~s base line (or Lines) as a reference. In this
                                    particular case,. no record whatever was made o£ the angular rela-
                                    tionship of the two larger triangular :footprints, which is a decided
                                    handicap ~n the analysis of the evidence.

                                       The Landing Gear Group of the Air Force Flight Dynamjcs Laboratory
                                       was asked to evaluate the subject depressions found in the vicinity
                                       of a UFO s:i ghting that occurred on July 30,. 1966. According to the
                    •
                                       investigators, the location of the depressions did not correspond
                                       to the area where the witness reported that the liFO -alighted. How-
                                       ever, the unusual shape and orientation of the depressions prompted
                                       further investigation following their discovery. The following are
                                       the conclusions and recommendations of FDFM:
                                                         ..
                                       Conclusions:

                                       1.  According to the investigating USAF Officer, the sand was defi-
                                       nitely compressed under load an~ not excavated as might have been
                                       done by a child playing on the beach.

                                       2.  Assuming that ~the depressions were made by an applied load and
                                       based on in~ction of the soil sample and the plaster-of-paris                                                              •

                                       ca~ting provided, the estimated weight that caused the two larger
                                       depressions was 750-1000 lbs. Since no inforwation was given regard-
                                       ing the size and depth of the snaaller {third) depression, no esti-
                                       mate regarding· the weight that may have rested on it can be given~                                                                                •


                                       3.  According to Mr. Max Groff, EWFRG, o         ivil Engineering,
                                       the outrigger stabilizing pads of certain a      construction equip-
                                       ment could leave a n inverted three-sided pyramld footprint shape
                                       similar to the ones £ound on Presque Isle. However, no vehicle
                                       tracks were observed in the vicinity of the footprint, which e:ffec-
                                       tively elimjnates this potential explanation.

                                       4. The layout o£ the three footprints showed no semblance o:f
                                       symmetry. If the third, smaller footprint is discounted, lines                                   •                 •           •

                                       extended through the apex and bisecting each of the two larger
                                       triangular footprints do not converge in a symmetrical manner.

                                                                                CONCLUSIONS


     1;       No evidence exists to relate the damp areas and the indentations found on

     the beach to the sighting.                                           Considering the identations, the following camnents
     are presented:                                                   •        -       •

                   •

              a.       No object could have made a stable landing without at least a third
     appendage.                                       •


              b.       Sand should have been a lot more canpressed for alleged landing.
              c.       No ground maneuver capability apparent.

              d.       Portions of ground indentations appear to have .been uncovered - not
     totally compressed, as should have been.

              e.       No definite sign of vehicle departing area in the sand.                                     No evidence

    · of heat blast or sand being disturbed by aerodynamic vehicle.

              f.       Rough weight calculations place weight of alleged object at approxi-
     mately 1500 lbs. tote.l weight.                                         This being a static load estimate calcualted
                          •

     anticipating· a two-legged object.                                                                              •

     indentation.             This wss attributed to the acrylic lacquer which was sprayed

     on the indentations prior to casting the mold.

              h.       Urine was distinctly present in the soil samples •

    Worthy of note is the fact that as object settled to the ground the car
    vibrated.   An obJect slowly descending onto a sandy area isn't likely to

    cause the vibration or a car approximately 300 - 400 yards in the distance,
    especially since the depth or the indentations were only about 4 - 5 inches
    1n the loose sand.


    Various discrepancies are noted throughout the available infol"Dl8tion.    These

    discrepancies are prevalent in the description of the alleged UFO and in the
    actual sequence of events as they occurred.    Considering these discrepancies,
